title: Monthly Retail Trade benchmark revision — retail sales and inventories restated on the 2023 and 2024 Annual Integrated Economic Survey (not-adjusted AND adjusted, same day)
source: EST: two Census primaries fetched direct 2026-09-06. census.gov/retail/index.html (HTTP 200, 743,183 bytes) announcements block, verbatim: "Intention to Revise: Monthly retail estimates are anticipated to be revised based on historical corrections and the results of the 2023 and 2024 Annual Integrated Economic Survey. Revised not adjusted estimates and corresponding adjusted estimates are tentatively scheduled for release on September 28, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. EDT." Corroborated on census.gov/mtis/index.html (HTTP 200, 684,348 bytes), which dates both halves of the same restatement in one sentence and both downstream MTIS editions. Stays `estimate` on three grounds, not one: Census's own word is "tentatively"; the date is ABSENT from census.gov/economic-indicators/calendar-listview.html (179 rows parsed 2026-09-06 — September runs 09-25 to 09-30, October runs 10-20 to 10-27), and no benchmark-revision row appears on ANY of the seven 2020-2026 schedules (1,135 rows, zero hits); and the lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN 2026-09-06 by this event's own initial research, after reading the single proposal for this id (`from-mtis-2026-12-16`), which is now shadowed. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE PREMISE THAT NAMED THIS EVENT, both from primary sources fetched this session. (1) THE `-nsa-` TOKEN IN THIS ID IS A MISNOMER. The discovering sweep read census.gov/mtis's "Revised not adjusted estimates and corresponding adjusted estimates are tentatively scheduled for release on September 28, 2026 and October 26, 2026, respectively" as mapping estimate TYPE to date — not-adjusted on 09-28, adjusted on 10-26. The two program pages refute that reading: census.gov/retail puts BOTH the not-adjusted and the "corresponding adjusted" retail estimates on 09-28, and census.gov/wholesale puts BOTH wholesale halves on 10-26. The "respectively" maps RETAIL and WHOLESALE, not NSA and SA. So 09-28 is the RETAIL benchmark revision in full, and mwts-benchmark-revision-2026-10-26 is the WHOLESALE one in full — two program halves of one restatement, not two sequential steps. The id is kept because it is the branch, ledger, tracking-issue and dedupe key; the title carries the truth. Registered as this event's FT--1. (2) DUPLICATE ID ON THE CALENDAR, NEEDS RESOLUTION. The mwts-benchmark-revision-2026-10-26 lane (merged 2026-09-06, PR #1768) independently proposed the SAME real-world release as `retail-benchmark-revision-2026-09-28` (impact medium). That proposal is a sibling lane's file, which this lane may neither delete nor overwrite (docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md), so from this merge the calendar carries one Census release under two ids, each drawing its own research lane forever. Recommended direction: retire `retail-benchmark-revision-2026-09-28` in favour of this id, which already carries the ledger, the forward tests and the [event-research] tracking issue — its slug is the more accurate of the two, but a slug is not worth breaking those links for. IMPACT FILED `low`, DIVERGING FROM THE SIBLING'S `medium`, and the divergence costs no coverage: no consensus forecast exists for a restatement, no new reference month is added, `symbols: []`, no macro-keyed house playbook exists, and the session class measures inert (SPY quarter-end-minus-2, n=66, median range 0.910% vs 0.904% baseline, permutation p=0.942). The `low` band still flips from 15+/30d to 0+/7d on 2026-09-13, so this event is next due 09-13 and gets roughly three more looks before the date. WHAT IT FEEDS: Census dates the downstream precisely — restated retail lands in the August-2026 MTIS edition of 2026-10-15 (schedule row A202610151000, reference A202608), the same morning as the high-impact 08:30 advance retail sales print (retail-sales-2026-10-15), which is the collision to keep straight. Research is not action: a restatement of 2023-2024 history is explicitly not a signal about the future, and this event licenses no entry on any date.
